319168895847f9d2c8e8b243fe5d9c5cca9f95ba.body:
For parameters satisfying
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} \(n\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Smoothness index.)} \(q\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope.)} \(L\geq 4\).
\end{itemize}
the common-map decision class and the point-indexed decision class of \cref{obj:def:cty-distance-decision-class,obj:def:point-indexed-distance-decision-class} satisfy
\[
\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\subsetneq \mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}.
\]

2f6e411e450f2d6b4c9c479315d22397b4dfc740.title: Planar Balls VC Bound
2f6e411e450f2d6b4c9c479315d22397b4dfc740.body:
For every finite set \(S\) of score points in \(\mathbb R^2\), if \(|S|\ge 4\), then \(S\) is not shattered by the class of closed Euclidean balls
\[
\{B_2(x,r): x\in\mathbb R^2,\ r\ge 0\}.
\]
Equivalently, no such \(S\) has the property that every subset of \(S\) can be written as \(S\cap B_2(x,r)\) for some center \(x\in\mathbb R^2\) and radius \(r\ge 0\).

a0cf8a8563ae35f04011a1723380d2462a0fd245.title: Angular Packing Certificate
a0cf8a8563ae35f04011a1723380d2462a0fd245.body:
For every integer \(q\geq 1\) and every envelope \(L\geq 4\), there exist constants
\[
c_0,c_1,c_w^-,c_w^+,c_{\mathrm{rad}},\alpha>0,
\qquad \alpha<\frac18,
\]
such that, for all sufficiently large \(n\), writing \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\), there are an integer \(M_n\), a radius \(w_n\), a mass \(m_n\), boundary points \(x_1,\ldots,x_{M_n}\), laws \(P_\omega\) indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), and values \(u_{j,0},u_{j,1}\) such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Packing size and scale.)}
\[
c_0 a_n^{-1/q}\leq M_n,
\qquad
c_w^- a_n^{1/q}\leq w_n\leq c_w^+ a_n^{1/q}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Boundary packing.)} With \(S=[-1/2,1/2]^2\), each \(x_j\) lies on \(\operatorname{bd}(S)\), and for \(i\neq j\),
\[
\|x_i-x_j\|_2\geq c_w^- a_n^{1/q}.
\]
The cells \(C_j=B_2(x_j,w_n)\cap S\) are pairwise disjoint.
\item \textbf{(Model class and support.)} For every \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^{M_n}\), the law \(P_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) and has covariate support \(S\).
\item \textbf{(Cell masses.)} For every \(\omega\) and every \(j\),
\[
P_\omega(X\in C_j)=m_n.
\]
\item \textbf{(Local dependence on one bit.)} If \(\omega_j=\omega'_j\), then the restricted laws of \((Y,X)\) on the cell \(C_j\) agree under \(P_\omega\) and \(P_{\omega'}\). The restricted laws of \((Y,X)\) on \(S\setminus\bigcup_{j=1}^{M_n}C_j\) are the same for all \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Boundary signal.)} For every \(\omega\) and \(j\),
\[
\mu_{P_\omega}(x_j)=u_{j,\omega_j},
\qquad
|u_{j,1}-u_{j,0}|\geq c_1 a_n.
\]
\item \textbf{(Radial invariance.)} Let \(\omega^{(j)}\) be \(\omega\) with coordinate \(j\) flipped. For every \(\omega\) and \(j\), the laws of \(\|X-x_j\|_2\) under \(P_\omega\) and \(P_{\omega^{(j)}}\) agree. Moreover, the corresponding one-point distance laws agree after restriction to radii \(z_2\geq c_{\mathrm{rad}}a_n\).
\item \textbf{(Compressed-distance KL bound.)} For every \(\omega\) and \(j\),
\[
\operatorname{KL}\!\left(
\mathcal L_{P_\omega}\{V_{n,P_\omega}(x_j)\},
\mathcal L_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}\{V_{n,P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\}
\right)
\leq \alpha\log M_n.
\]
\end{itemize}

d518e2e3abf931019776adf27f24643cdbe07794.title: Winsorization Bias Bound
d518e2e3abf931019776adf27f24643cdbe07794.body:
Let \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-class}\), and let \(B\geq 1\).  Define
\[
\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}.
\]
Then, for each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and each \(x\in\mathcal X_P\), under the selected conditional law of \(Y(t)\) given \(X=x\),
\[
\left|
\int y\,dP_{Y(t)\mid X=x}(y)
-
\int \psi_B(y)\,dP_{Y(t)\mid X=x}(y)
\right|
\leq L B^{-3}.
\]

6312df36808d623771bee41fdd39f4d263da3943.title: Winsorized Score Maximal Bound
6312df36808d623771bee41fdd39f4d263da3943.body:
Fix a nonnegative integer \(p\) and a real number \(L\).  There is a constant
\(C=C(p,L)>0\) such that the following holds for every real \(\nu\).

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Law class.)} The law \(P\) belongs to the A1/A2 class
\(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) of \cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-class}.
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and clipping.)} The bandwidth and winsorization level satisfy
\(0<h\leq L^{-1}\) and \(B\geq 1\).
\end{itemize}

Let \(P^n\) denote the \(n\)-fold i.i.d. law of the potential-outcome observations.
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), let the winsorized centered local-polynomial
score be the vector whose \(j\)th coordinate is
\[
\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h,j}
  - \mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h,j}\right],
\]
where the empirical score uses the uniform kernel, the polynomial basis \(r_p\), bandwidth \(h\),
and the clipped outcome transform \(\psi_B\), centered around the corresponding population score.
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{P^n}^{*}\!\left[
\sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
\left\|
\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h}
-\mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h}\right]
\right\|
\right]
\leq
C\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{\log(B/h)}{n h^2}}
+
\frac{B\log(B/h)}{n h^2}
\right\}.
\]

1602707ce38b38ce760c1aa4d6015350a94013a9.title: Point-Indexed Log Converse
1602707ce38b38ce760c1aa4d6015350a94013a9.body:
For every integer \(p\ge 0\), there exists a real number \(L_0=L_0(p)\) with \(L_0\ge 48\) such that, for every \(\nu\ge 2\) and every \(L\ge L_0\), there exists a constant \(c=c(p,\nu,L)>0\) satisfying the following conclusions.  Let \(R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\) denote the signed-distance minimax risk in \(\cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-outer-risk}\), and let \(R^{12,\pm,\mathrm{fix}}_n(p,\nu,L)\) be the same infimum over known-geometry point-indexed decision rules and the same worst-case outer-expected interface sup-loss, with the law supremum further restricted to laws in \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) satisfying the fixed hard-geometry condition.  Writing \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty} a_n^{-1}R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)
=
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n},
\]
and
\[
c
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n},
\qquad
c
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm,\mathrm{fix}}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n}.
\]

9b3e22e784d3f0aed52c8250f6c570daf4d03382.title: Rectangle Angular Hypercube
9b3e22e784d3f0aed52c8250f6c570daf4d03382.body:
For every integer \(p\geq 0\), there is a constant \(L_0=L_0(p)\geq 48\) such that, for every \(\nu\geq 2\) and every \(L\geq L_0\), there are constants \(c,A,C,C_0>0\), with \(2C<A\) when \(p=0\), and a constant \(\delta_0>0\) such that the following construction is available for every \(0<\Delta\leq\delta_0\).  Writing \(q=p+1\), there exist an integer \(M\), constants \(w,\rho>0\), points \(x_1,\ldots,x_M\), laws \(P_\omega\) indexed by \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), and probability laws \(Q_{j,b}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,M\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\), satisfying:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Size and calibration.)}
\[
M\geq c\Delta^{-1/q},\qquad
w=A\Delta^{1/q},\qquad
\rho=\frac{\pi w^2}{36}.
\]
\item \textbf{(Common geometry.)} The support is \(\mathcal X=[-3,3]^2\), the treated region is \(\mathcal A_1=[-1,1]\times[0,2]\), the control region is \(\mathcal A_0=\mathcal X\setminus\mathcal A_1\), the boundary is \(\mathcal B=\partial\mathcal A_1\), the metric is Euclidean distance, and the kernel is \(K_\square\).  The points \(x_j\) lie on the middle of the bottom edge, and the disks \(S_j=B_2(x_j,w)\) are contained in \(\mathcal X\), pairwise separated by distance at least \(2w\), and pairwise disjoint.
\item \textbf{(Class membership.)} For every \(\omega\in\{0,1\}^M\), the law \(P_\omega\) belongs to \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) with the common geometry above.
\item \textbf{(Bit structure.)} For every \(\omega\) and \(j\),
\[
P_\omega\{z:\operatorname{score}(z)\in S_j\}=\rho.
\]
The restriction of \(P_\omega\) to \(S_j\) depends on \(\omega\) only through \(\omega_j\), and the restriction of \(P_\omega\) outside \(\bigcup_{j=1}^M S_j\) is common across all \(\omega\).
\item \textbf{(Signed-observation laws.)} Conditional on \(\operatorname{score}(Z)\in S_j\), the one-observation signed-distance law at \(x_j\) under \(P_\omega\) is \(Q_{j,\omega_j}\).
\item \textbf{(Signal separation.)} If two vertices agree in coordinate \(j\), then their treatment-effect targets at \(x_j\) agree.  Flipping coordinate \(j\) changes the treatment-effect target at \(x_j\) by exactly \(\Delta\):
\[
\left|\tau_{P_\omega}(x_j)-\tau_{P_{\omega^{(j)}}}(x_j)\right|=\Delta.
\]
\item \textbf{(Local comparison laws.)} For each \(j\), the laws \(Q_{j,0}\) and \(Q_{j,1}\) have the same signed-distance marginal, agree outside the event \(0<D^\pm_{P,x_j}<2C\Delta\), and obey the two Kullback--Leibler bounds
\[
\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq C_0\frac{\Delta^4}{w^2},
\qquad
\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,1},Q_{j,0})\leq C_0\frac{\Delta^4}{w^2}.
\]
\end{itemize}

1e91b4d907b557e207229fee000ba7f4a6681edf.title: Expected Outer Upper Bound
1e91b4d907b557e207229fee000ba7f4a6681edf.body:
Let \(p\geq 0\) be an integer, let \(\nu\geq 2\), and let \(L\geq 4\).  Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Distance identification.)}  For every A1/A2 law \(P\), every distance map \(d\), and every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\) satisfying the CTY identification assumptions at order \(p\), there are signed-distance conditional-mean versions \(\theta_1,\theta_0:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) and one-sided limits \(\theta_1(0+)\) and \(\theta_0(0-)\) such that
\[
\tau_P(x)=\theta_1(0+)-\theta_0(0-).
\]
\item \textbf{(Uniform first-order bias.)}  There is a constant \(C_b>0\), depending on \(p\) and \(L\), such that for every \(\nu'\geq 2\) and every positive antitone deterministic bandwidth sequence \(h_n\) with \(h_n\to0\) and \(n h_n^2\to\infty\),
\[
\limsup_{n\to\infty}
\mathrm{BiasRatio}_{p,\nu',L}(h_n)\leq C_b .
\]
\item \textbf{(Expected maximal bounds.)}  There is a constant \(C_m>0\) such that, for every positive deterministic bandwidth sequence \(h_n\) with \(h_n\to0\) and
\[
\frac{n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h_n^2}{\log(h_n^{-1})}\to\infty,
\]
the following bounds hold for all sufficiently large \(n\), uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\):
\[
\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\mathrm{GramDev}_{n,p,P}(h_n)\right]
\leq
C_m
\sqrt{\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n h_n^2}},
\]
and
\[
\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[\mathrm{ScoreDev}_{n,p,P}(h_n)\right]
\leq
C_m\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n h_n^2}}
+
\frac{\log(h_n^{-1})}{n^{(1+\nu)/(2+\nu)}h_n^2}
\right\}.
\]
\end{itemize}
With \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:frontier-rates}\), take the bandwidth \(h_n=a_n\) and the winsorization level \(B_n=a_n^{-1/3}\) in the winsorized, Gram-stabilized signed-distance local-polynomial estimator clipped to \([-2L,2L]\).  Then there are constants \(C>0\) and \(N\) such that, for every \(n\geq N\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
\mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
\sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}
\left|\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h_n}(x)-\tau_P(x)\right|
\right]
\leq C a_n .
\]

1aa35e06b2fb963e5a7249c77acdcbccb334dd98.title: Nonparametric law class $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)$
1aa35e06b2fb963e5a7249c77acdcbccb334dd98.body:
The class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\) consists of all laws \(P\) satisfying the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling.)} For every \(n\), \((Y_i,X_i)_{i=1}^n\) are independently and identically distributed under \(P\) in \(\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^2\).
\item \textbf{(Design.)} The covariate \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on its compact support \(\mathcal X_P\subseteq[-L,L]^2\), such that
\[
L^{-1}\leq \inf_{x\in\mathcal X_P} f_P(x)
\leq \sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P} f_P(x)\leq L,
\]
and \(\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a rectifiable curve.
\item \textbf{(Regression.)} The conditional mean
\[
\mu_P(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y\mid X=x]
\]
belongs to \(\mathcal H^q(\mathcal X_P,L)\).
\item \textbf{(Variance.)} The conditional variance
\[
\sigma_P^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y\mid X=x)
\]
is continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\) and satisfies
\[
L^{-1}\leq \sigma_P^2(x)\leq L
\]
for every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\).
\end{itemize}
Equivalently,
\[
\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)
=
\{P:\text{\(P\) satisfies conditions \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(iv)}\) above}\}.
\]

35c2f137f854617a1f8e9e69122db18821d753db.title: Distance data $V_{n,P}(x)$
35c2f137f854617a1f8e9e69122db18821d753db.body:

\[
V_{n,P}(x)
=
\bigl((Y_i,\lVert X_i-x\rVert_2):1\leq i\leq n\bigr).
\]

25b78e7eaf345b52bc4fb67ec40d617a745fb4cb.title: Point-indexed class $\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}$
25b78e7eaf345b52bc4fb67ec40d617a745fb4cb.body:
The point-indexed decision class is
\[
\mathcal T_n^{\mathrm{PI}}
=
\left\{
\widehat\mu_n^{\mathrm{PI}}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{there exists a family }\{T_{n,x}:x\in\mathbb R^2\}
\text{ selected independently of }P,\\
T_{n,x}:(\mathbb R\times[0,\infty))^n\to\mathbb R
\text{ is Borel measurable for every fixed }x,\\
\widehat\mu_{n,P}^{\mathrm{PI}}(x)=T_{n,x}(V_{n,P}(x))
\text{ for every }P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{NP}}(L,q)\\
\text{and every }x\in\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal X_P)
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
This class consists exactly of such law-independent fixed-\(x\) Borel sections.

d21088df2eca67442dbdae481996aa52944d99e5.body:

\[

\]

9c567dbd6ea4bd10dcdd6e0a8768f39022c855bd.title: Known geometry \(G_P\)
9c567dbd6ea4bd10dcdd6e0a8768f39022c855bd.body:
For a member law \(P\), the known design object is
\[
G_P=(\mathcal X_P,\mathcal A_{0,P},\mathcal A_{1,P},\mathcal B_P,d_P,K_\square),
\]
where \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) are a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\),
\[
\mathcal B_P
=
\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{0,P})
\cap
\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{1,P})
\subset
\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P),
\]
and
\[
d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2.
\]

1ea2f1900ca91640b36abfbbdb42b16410f4ad0b.title: Signed-distance data \(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)\)
1ea2f1900ca91640b36abfbbdb42b16410f4ad0b.body:
For \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), define the signed distance
\[
D^{\pm}_{P,x}
=
\{\mathbf 1(X\in\mathcal A_{1,P})-\mathbf 1(X\in\mathcal A_{0,P})\}
\lVert X-x\rVert_2
\]
and the signed-distance sample
\[
U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)=((Y_i,D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}):1\leq i\leq n).
\]

474d0c91dcc48dc0fe5d541707b1ee26029f76c4.title: A1/A2 law class \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\)
474d0c91dcc48dc0fe5d541707b1ee26029f76c4.body:
For integers \(p\geq0\), real numbers \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\), let \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) be the set of laws \(P\) satisfying the following conditions.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Sampling and consistency.)} For every \(n\), the vectors \((Y_i(0),Y_i(1),X_i)\), \(1\leq i\leq n\), are independently and identically distributed,
\[
T=\mathbf 1\{X\in\mathcal A_{1,P}\},
\qquad
Y=TY(1)+(1-T)Y(0).
\]

\item \textbf{(Rectangular support and density.)} The support has the form
\[
\mathcal X_P=[\underline x_P,\overline x_P]^2\subseteq[-L,L]^2.
\]
The variable \(X\) has a Lebesgue density \(f_P\), continuous on \(\mathcal X_P\), such that
\[
L^{-1}\leq f_P(x)\leq L,
\qquad x\in\mathcal X_P.
\]

\item \textbf{(Smooth potential-outcome regressions.)} For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the regression
\[
\mu_{t,P}(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y(t)\mid X=x]
\]
has a \(C^{p+1}\) extension to an open neighborhood of \(\mathcal X_P\), and
\[
\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\in\mathcal X_P}|\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)|
+
\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq p}\sup_{x\neq z\in\mathcal X_P}
{|\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(x)-\partial^\alpha\mu_{t,P}(z)|
\over
\lVert x-z\rVert_2}
\leq L.
\]

\item \textbf{(Conditional variances.)} For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), the conditional variance
\[
\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)=\operatorname{Var}_P(Y(t)\mid X=x)
\]
is continuous and satisfies
\[
L^{-1}\leq\sigma^2_{t,P}(x)\leq L,
\qquad x\in\mathcal X_P.
\]

\item \textbf{(Moment envelope.)} For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and every \(x\in\mathcal X_P\),
\[
\mathbb E_P[|Y(t)|^{2+\nu}\mid X=x]\leq L.
\]

\item \textbf{(Assignment geometry.)} The sets \(\mathcal A_{0,P}\) and \(\mathcal A_{1,P}\) form a Borel partition of \(\mathcal X_P\), and their known common interface \(\mathcal B_P\subset\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P)\) is a compact rectifiable curve satisfying
\[
L^{-1}\leq\mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\leq L.
\]

\item \textbf{(Metric, kernel, and VC bound.)} The known metric and kernel are
\[
d_P(x,z)=\lVert x-z\rVert_2,
\qquad
K_\square.
\]
The collection
\[
\{\{z\in\mathcal X_P:\lVert z-x\rVert_2\leq r\}:x\in\mathcal X_P,\ r\geq0\}
\]
is a VC class with VC index at most four.

\item \textbf{(Population Gram lower bound.)} Put
\[
r_p(u)=(1,u,\ldots,u^p)^\top,
\qquad
I_1=[0,\infty),
\qquad
I_0=(-\infty,0),
\]
and
\[
\Psi_{t,P,x}(h)
=
\mathbb E_P\!\left[
{1\over h^2}\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}
K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)
r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h)^\top
\right].
\]
For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
\lambda_{\min}(\Psi_{t,P,x}(h))\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Small-bandwidth arm mass.)} For every \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\), every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and both \(t\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
{1\over h^2}\int_{\mathcal A_{t,P}}
K_\square(\{(2t-1)\lVert z-x\rVert_2\}/h)\,dz
\geq L^{-1}.
\]

\item \textbf{(Distance-slice density.)} For every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), both \(t\in\{0,1\}\), and every \(0<s\leq L^{-1}\), the one-dimensional Hausdorff integral of \(f_P\) over
\[
\{z\in\mathcal A_{t,P}:\lVert z-x\rVert_2=s\}
\]
is finite and strictly positive.
\end{itemize}

This class is the displayed \(L\)-uniformized Euclidean-distance, uniform-kernel specialization of the two baseline smoothness and design conditions, augmented by the displayed envelope restrictions and quantitative small-bandwidth thresholds.

38019687e571cab6f398f17e970f3713eb0ab440.title: Known-geometry rules \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\)
38019687e571cab6f398f17e970f3713eb0ab440.body:
Let \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\) be the class of rules for which there is one collection
\[
\{T_{n,G,x}:G\text{ is an admissible known geometry},\ x\in\mathbb R^2\}
\]
selected independently of the unknown member law, such that every fixed \((G,x)\) section is a Borel map from \((\mathbb R\times\mathbb R)^n\) to \(\mathbb R\) and, for every \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), every \(p\geq0\), and every \(x\in\mathcal B_P\),
\[
\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)
=
T_{n,G_P,x}(U^{\pm}_{n,P}(x)).
\]
The imposed regularity is fixed-\((G,x)\) Borel measurability of each section.

de485fbcbb87f7697fd4ded54be7da40d34116bd.title: Signed-distance minimax risk \(R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\)
de485fbcbb87f7697fd4ded54be7da40d34116bd.body:
For an extended nonnegative function \(Z\), define its outer expectation under \(P\) by
\[
 \mathbb E_P^*[Z]
 =
 \inf\{\mathbb E_P[W]: W \text{ is extended nonnegative and measurable, and } W\geq Z \text{ pointwise}\}.
\]
For \(p\geq0\), the signed-distance minimax risk is
\[
 R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)
 =
 \inf_{\widehat\tau_n\in\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)}
 \mathbb E_P^*\!\left[
 \sup_{x\in\mathcal B_P}|\widehat\tau_{n,P}(x)-\tau_P(x)|
 \right].
\]

d27c6d48b2ed4cb59996c9c7f07e5131bf4253c5.title: Stabilized local-polynomial estimator \(\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\)
d27c6d48b2ed4cb59996c9c7f07e5131bf4253c5.body:
For \(B>0\), define the winsorization map
\[
 \psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}.
\]
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(h>0\), set
\[
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top
\]
and, with \(B(h)=h^{-1/3}\),
\[
 \widehat m^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)\psi_{B(h)}(Y_i).
\]
Define
\[
 \widehat\beta^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)^{-1}\widehat m^B_{t,x}(h),
 & \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h))\geq(2L)^{-1},\\
 0,
 & \lambda_{\min}(\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h))<(2L)^{-1}.
 \end{cases}
\]
With \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), define
\[
 \widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =
 \Pi_{[-2L,2L]}\!\left\{
 e_1^\top(\widehat\beta^B_{1,x}(h)-\widehat\beta^B_{0,x}(h))
 \right\}.
\]
At the theorem bandwidth \(h_n=a_n\), the winsorization level is
\[
 B_n=B(h_n)=a_n^{-1/3}.
\]
For every \(p\geq0\), this construction gives a fixed, law-independent, jointly Borel member of \(\mathcal T^{12,\pm}_n\).

6e8e6620ea4372ea11e44132ac80dfc4de777f04.title: Coordinatewise overlap product
6e8e6620ea4372ea11e44132ac80dfc4de777f04.body:
Assume the following conditions.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Spaces.)} The spaces carrying \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M,S_1,\ldots,S_M\) are standard Borel.
\item \textbf{(Binary coordinates.)} The variables \(\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M\) are independent and uniformly distributed on \(\{0,1\}\).
\item \textbf{(Conditional product structure.)} Conditionally on \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\), the variables \(Z_0,Z_1,\ldots,Z_M\) are independent, the law of \(Z_j\) depends only on \(\Omega_j\) for \(1\leq j\leq M\), and the law of \(Z_0\) is independent of \((\Omega_1,\ldots,\Omega_M)\).
\item \textbf{(Compressed coordinate decoding.)} For each \(j\), \(S_j\) is a measurable compression of \(Z_j\), the decoder \(\widehat\Omega_j\) is measurable with respect to \((S_j,Z_{-j},Z_0)\), and
\[
 Q_{j,b}=\mathcal L(S_j\mid\Omega_j=b),
 \qquad
 \rho_j=1-\lVert Q_{j,0}-Q_{j,1}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
\end{itemize}
Then every such decentralized decoder satisfies
\[
 \Pr\{\widehat\Omega_j=\Omega_j\text{ for every }j\}
 \leq
 \frac12\left\{1+\prod_{j=1}^M(1-\rho_j)\right\}.
\]
In particular, if \(\operatorname{KL}(Q_{j,0},Q_{j,1})\leq\kappa\log M\) for all \(j\) and for a fixed \(\kappa<1\), then
\[
 \Pr\{\text{at least one decoding error}\}
 \geq
 \frac12\left[1-\exp\{-M^{1-\kappa}/2\}\right].
\]
Along any sequence with \(M=M_n\to\infty\) and fixed \(\kappa<1\), this lower bound is \(1/2-o(1)\).

0445ef746435126d23130c303a8681d5dc45057b.title: Point-Indexed Log Converse

d6dec2f79a0586789538ff1af3262d1bfa44841d.title: Point-Indexed Log Converse
d6dec2f79a0586789538ff1af3262d1bfa44841d.body:
For every integer \(p\ge 0\), there exists a real number \(L_0=L_0(p)\) with \(L_0\ge 48\) such that, under the following conditions,
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Moment exponent.)} The moment exponent satisfies \(\nu\ge 2\).
\item \textbf{(Envelope size.)} The envelope satisfies \(L\ge L_0\).
\item \textbf{(Decision rules.)} The risk \(R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\) is the signed-distance minimax risk in \cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-outer-risk}, formed over law-independent known-geometry point-indexed Borel sections.
\item \textbf{(Fixed hard geometry.)} The risk \(R^{12,\pm,\mathrm{fix}}_n(p,\nu,L)\) is the same infimum over known-geometry point-indexed decision rules and the same worst-case outer-expected interface sup-loss, with the law supremum restricted to laws in \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) satisfying the fixed hard-geometry condition: one fixed support, one fixed known assignment rectangle, and one fixed known interior treatment boundary.
\end{itemize}
there exists a constant \(c=c(p,\nu,L)>0\) such that, writing \(a_n=(\log n/n)^{1/4}\),
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty} a_n^{-1}R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)
=
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n},
\]
and
\[
c
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n},
\qquad
c
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}{R^{12,\pm,\mathrm{fix}}_n(p,\nu,L)\over a_n}.
\]

8949921d7198b75537f5218370a8b8b361cdc6f6.title: Winsorized Score Bound
8949921d7198b75537f5218370a8b8b361cdc6f6.body:
Fix a nonnegative integer \(p\) and a real number \(L\).  There is a constant
\(C=C(p,L)>0\) such that, for every real \(\nu\), the following holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Law class.)} The law \(P\) belongs to the A1/A2 class
\(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) of \cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-class}.
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and clipping.)} The bandwidth and winsorization level satisfy
\(0<h\leq L^{-1}\) and \(B\geq 1\).
\end{itemize}

Let \(P^n\) denote the \(n\)-fold i.i.d. law of the potential-outcome observations.
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), define the vector-valued winsorized score
fluctuation \(\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)\) by
\[
\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)
=
{1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 \left[\psi_B(Y_i)-r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\right].
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{P^n}^{*}\!\left[
 \sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
 \left\|\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)-\mathbb E_{P^n}\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)\right\|
 \right]
\leq
C\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{\log(B/h)}{n h^2}}
+
\frac{B\log(B/h)}{n h^2}
\right\}.
\]

13c8db6beaf4b5515fcc72dd25cffd7bad9d0d12.title: CTY identification assumptions \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\)
13c8db6beaf4b5515fcc72dd25cffd7bad9d0d12.body:
A law \(P\) satisfies the CTY identification assumptions with parameters \(p\geq0\), \(\nu\geq2\), and \(L\geq4\) when
\[
P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L).
\]
Equivalently, the potential-outcome law \((Y(0),Y(1),X)\), the known Borel partition \((\mathcal A_{0,P},\mathcal A_{1,P})\), the interface \(\mathcal B_P\), the Euclidean metric, the uniform kernel \(K_\square\), the conditional mean and variance regularity, the pointwise conditional \((2+\nu)\)-moment envelope, the VC ball condition, the local-polynomial Gram lower bound, and the one-dimensional Hausdorff-section positivity conditions satisfy clauses \(\mathrm{(i)}\)--\(\mathrm{(x)}\) in the definition of \(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\).

9d0a38b301cfbba8592c9767b29e03f27951a946.title: Gram deviation \(\mathrm{GramDev}_{n,p,P}(h)\)

6d3f67d5041406b87a678356d5e5f0fba761c30e.title: Winsorized score \(\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h,j}\)
6d3f67d5041406b87a678356d5e5f0fba761c30e.body:
For a law \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), sample size \(n\), arm \(t\in\{0,1\}\), interface point \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), bandwidth \(h>0\), winsorization level \(B>0\), and coordinate \(j\in\{0,\ldots,p\}\), the winsorized local-polynomial residual score is the \(P^n\)-random variable
\[
\operatorname{score}^{B}_{t,x,h,j}
=
\frac{1}{n h^2}
\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}
K_\square\!\left(\frac{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}}{h}\right)
r_p\!\left(\frac{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}}{h}\right)_j
\left[
\psi_B(Y_i)
-
r_p\!\left(\frac{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}}{h}\right)^\top
\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)
\right],
\]
where \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\) is the unwinsorized population local-polynomial coefficient at \((t,x,h)\).

f7e0c0fab334820ecea05e88d017fc8ff925b292.title: Stabilized local-polynomial estimator \(\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}\)
f7e0c0fab334820ecea05e88d017fc8ff925b292.body:
For \(B\in\mathbb R\), define the winsorization map by
\[
\psi_B(y)=\operatorname{sign}(y)\min\{|y|,B\}.
\]
For each \(t\in\{0,1\}\), query point \(x\), and bandwidth \(h\), define
\[
\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top .
\]
With \(B(h)=h^{-1/3}\), define
\[
\widehat m^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 {1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
 \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
 r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)\psi_{B(h)}(Y_i).
\]
The stabilized coefficient is
\[
\widehat\beta^B_{t,x}(h)
 =
 \begin{cases}
 \widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)^{-1}\widehat m^B_{t,x}(h),
 & \text{if }\forall v\in\mathbb R^{p+1},\ (2L)^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^p v_j^2\leq v^\top\widehat\Psi_{t,x}(h)v,\\
 0,
 & \text{otherwise.}
 \end{cases}
\]
With \(e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)^\top\), the clipped signed-distance local-polynomial treatment-effect estimator is
\[
\widehat\tau^{12,\mathrm{LP}}_{n,h}(x)
 =
 \max\!\left\{-2L,\min\!\left\{2L,
 e_1^\top(\widehat\beta^B_{1,x}(h)-\widehat\beta^B_{0,x}(h))
 \right\}\right\}.
\]

22c953fae0704f5db5f2f0ee2345acbcb5b0ddfd.title: Raw signed-distance moments
22c953fae0704f5db5f2f0ee2345acbcb5b0ddfd.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), and \(j=0,\ldots,p\), define the raw empirical signed-distance moment and its population counterpart at bandwidth \(h_n\) by
\[
\widehat m_{t,x,j}(h_n)=\frac{1}{n h_n^2}\sum_{i=1}^n \mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h_n)r_{p,j}(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h_n)Y_i
\]
and
\[
m_{t,P,x,j}(h_n)=\mathbb E_P\!\left[h_n^{-2}\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x}\in I_t\}K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h_n)r_{p,j}(D^{\pm}_{P,x}/h_n)Y\right].
\]

389f69dffa878182fb2cfc9d05fe7fb7e7f61e4f.title: Winsorized Score Maximal Bound
389f69dffa878182fb2cfc9d05fe7fb7e7f61e4f.body:
Fix a nonnegative integer \(p\) and a real number \(L\).  There is a constant
\(C=C(p,L)>0\) such that, for every real \(\nu\), the following statement holds.

\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Law class.)} The law \(P\) belongs to
\(\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\) of \cref{obj:def:cty-a1-a2-class}.
\item \textbf{(Sample size.)} The sample size satisfies \(n\geq 1\).
\item \textbf{(Bandwidth and winsorization.)} The bandwidth and winsorization
level satisfy \(0<h\leq L^{-1}\) and \(B\geq 1\).
\end{itemize}

Let \(P^n\) denote the \(n\)-fold i.i.d. law of the potential-outcome observations.
For \(t\in\{0,1\}\) and \(x\in\mathcal B_P\), let \(\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)\) solve
the unwinsorized population normal equations, and define the winsorized empirical
local-polynomial score vector
\[
\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)
=
{1\over nh^2}\sum_{i=1}^n
\mathbf 1\{D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}\in I_t\}
K_\square(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)
\left[
\psi_B(Y_i(t))
-
r_p(D^{\pm}_{P,x,i}/h)^\top\beta^*_{t,P,x}(h)
\right].
\]
Then
\[
\mathbb E_{P^n}^{*}\!\left[
\sup_{t\in\{0,1\},\,x\in\mathcal B_P}
\left\|
\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)
-
\mathbb E_{P^n}\!\left[\widehat O^B_{t,x}(h)\right]
\right\|
\right]
\leq
C\left\{
\sqrt{\frac{\log(B/h)}{n h^2}}
+
\frac{B\log(B/h)}{n h^2}
\right\}.
\]

e73b5306e3bb7dbffd8f67121b4985a9925ec76d.title: Known treatment interface \(\mathcal B_P\)
e73b5306e3bb7dbffd8f67121b4985a9925ec76d.body:
For \(P\in\mathcal P_{12}(p,\nu,L)\), the known treatment interface is
\[
\mathcal B_P
=
\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{0,P})\cap
\operatorname{bd}(\mathcal A_{1,P})
\subset
\operatorname{int}(\mathcal X_P).
\]
It is a compact rectifiable curve satisfying
\[
L^{-1}\leq \mathcal H^1(\mathcal B_P)\leq L.
\]
